Well, Dr. Smith, I’m here because... for months now, I’ve been seeing the exact same pattern. My sister’s appointments keep getting moved around, her bills show up completely wrong, and people just conveniently 'forget' to call me back. 

It’s funny because at my job—I supervise the administrative support team at a regional office—if one of my clerks 'forgot' to return an important call, I’d have them written up. Just last week, I had a new temp, Brenda, who couldn't even transfer a call properly. She had this awful floral perfume on, too, gave me a terrible headache the whole afternoon.

I know they’re keeping information from me on purpose. They are actively trying to push me out of all the decisions regarding her. It’s just like my neighbor when he put up that new privacy fence without even checking the property line or talking to the HOA... people just scheme behind your back and expect you not to notice. Documented proof? Like logs and records? No, absolutely not. I wouldn't believe it for a second. I mean, I'm here because for months now I've been seeing the exact same pattern. My sister's appointments get moved, the bills show up wrong, people conveniently 'forget' to call me back. She was supposed to be logging the incoming mail, and I caught her backdating the entry stamps because she'd let a whole stack sit on her desk for three days. Three days! In a busy office, that is an eternity. We had to implement a whole new tracking system after that. I spent an entire weekend designing the new spreadsheet. I even color-coded the priority levels. My husband at the time—we're divorced now, he moved to Florida—he complained that I was working on a Sunday, but I told him, 'If you want things done right, you have to put in the time.' He never really understood my work ethic. He was more the type to just sit on the couch and watch golf all weekend. I never understood the appeal of golf. It's just walking around a big lawn, hitting a little ball. 

But anyway, no, a logbook wouldn't change my mind. I know what they're doing. They're trying to push me out, and a piece of paper isn't going to convince me otherwise.

Scheming? Oh, no, heavens no. It’s strictly the people at my sister's facility. Doctor: Have you ever felt that the staff might be acting maliciously because of something specific you did or said, or do you think they are doing this for some other reason?

Patient: Oh, no, it's not because of anything I did. I've been perfectly reasonable. I think they just want to avoid accountability, and I'm the only one holding their feet to the fire. They want to cut corners and not have anyone checking their work. 

Speaking of checking work, I had to completely redo the quarterly supply inventory at the office last week because my new assistant, Brenda, just guessed at the numbers instead of actually counting the toner cartridges. She’s very sweet, but she’s just not detail-oriented. She brought in these amazing homemade blueberry muffins on Tuesday, though. The tops were perfectly crusty with that coarse sugar on them. I haven't baked muffins in years. I used to have this heavy cast-iron muffin pan that belonged to my grandmother. It weighed an absolute ton, but it baked everything so evenly. Well, I suppose so, yes. I just believe things should be done correctly. If there's a rule or a procedure, it's there for a reason, right? Like at the office, I expect my clerks to follow the manual to the letter. It's not about being difficult, it's about efficiency. \n\nSpeaking of efficiency, I was at the grocery store yesterday, and the cashier—this young kid, probably still in high school—was bagging my groceries so haphazardly. He put the raw chicken right on top of the fresh produce! I had to stop him and explain cross-contamination. He rolled his eyes at me, can you believe that? The lack of respect for basic hygiene is just astounding these days. It reminds me of this restaurant I went to last month, an Italian place. The waiter brought out my pasta, and I swear the plate was chipped. I sent it back, of course. You can't serve food on chipped china, it's a health hazard. They ended up comping my dessert, a tiramisu, which honestly was a bit soggy anyway. I make a much better tiramisu at home. The secret is to dip the ladyfingers very quickly, just a quick dunk in the espresso, otherwise, they get mushy. \n\nBut, um, yes, I do like things done right. Whether it's at work or anywhere else, I just think if you're going to do something, you should do it properly.\n\nDoctor: If your sister's care team showed you documented proof—like time-stamped call logs or the original clerical records—that these errors were genuine mistakes and not intentional, do you think that evidence could change your mind, or would you still be certain they were done on purpose?\n\nPatient: Documented proof? Like logs and records? No, absolutely not. I wouldn't believe it for a second. I mean, I'm here because for months now I've been seeing the exact same pattern. My sister's appointments get moved, the bills show up wrong, people conveniently 'forget' to call me back. Even when we were kids, if there was any kind of conflict, he would just disappear into his room and build those little model airplanes. He had hundreds of them hanging from his ceiling. I always wondered how my mother dusted them. She was meticulous about dusting. She used this lemon oil polish that smelled so strong, it would give me a headache if I stayed in the room too long. If a clerk misfiles a report, I need to know exactly *why* it happened, not just that it was an accident. I always thought maroon was such a dreary color for a car. My first car was a bright yellow Datsun. Oh, I loved that little car.
